subject: Request: per-route SLO-drift alerts + token-cost slicing for console
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: cloud-partner@fastcloud.io

Subject: Request: per-route SLO-drift alerts + token-cost slicing for console

Team —

Quick ask from Product (console observability): Acme flagged that their monthly bill spiked by ~18% tied to a handful of routes where tail latency and token usage drifted after a recent rollout. They want a way in Console to: 

- surface per-route token-cost breakdown (day/week) by customer slice
- detect SLO drift for a route (error/latency) and notify owners with a suggested rollback or fallback
- pair cost anomaly windows with example traces/requests (sampled) for quick RCA

Attached is a small export from Acme (sample_query_export.csv) and a proposed alert matrix (proposed-alert-matrix.xlsx). High-level asks: 

1) Prioritize a lightweight ‘route card’ view in Console that shows: 24h token spend, 95/99 latency, request count, and top contributing customer slices.
2) Add an auto-triggered SLO-drift alert that includes the last 10 sampled traces and a one-click route fallback to a cheaper quantized variant (if available).
3) For billing/CS teams: a per-route cost-export in CSV/JSON with hop-to-customer mapping.

Questions: which of these are product UI changes vs infra-level telemetry? rough estimate of effort? any blocker for shipping an MVP within the next 6 weeks?

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: sample_query_export.csv (csv, 24KB)
Attachment: proposed-alert-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 46KB)

Subject: Re: Request: per-route SLO-drift alerts + token-cost slicing for console

Diego —

Love the clarity on the asks. Quick alignment from Console PM perspective:

- UI: ‘route card’ is straightforward as a new tile on the Route detail page. We can ship a read-only MVP that pulls existing metrics (tokens, p95/p99 latency) and links to sampled traces.
- Alerts: SLO-drift alert needs two pieces: detection (signal pipeline) + a templated notification with rollback/call-to-action. We should avoid building rollback automation in week one — instead provide a one-click ‘suggested action’ that opens the route rollback flow.
- Exports: CSV/JSON export is in scope for the CS workflow; likely requires enrichment mapping request -> tenant id at ingestion time.

Can Marcus/infra comment on sampling retention and how easy it is to return the last N traces for a route? Also: timeline-wise I can commit Console UI design and a feature flagged rollout if we get a small infra contract (2-3 sprints).

Proposed next step: 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to triage and split into tech backlog items (ENG-1327). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

— Ava
Ava Chen

On Wed, May 5, 2027 at 11:02 AM Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus/infra comment on sampling retention and how easy it is to return the last N traces for a route?

Short answer: feasible but with trade-offs. A few notes from infra: 

- Sampling: we already persist sampled traces for a rolling 30d window for top-tier customers; for the rest we currently keep ~72h. We can expose the last N traces for a route if we increase retention or add a fast index by route-id. Both have cost implications.
- Token-cost slice: we have token attribution per request in raw logs, but the join from request -> customer slice is done downstream in the billing pipeline. We can wire a simplified join at query-time for the Console export (best-effort, eventual consistency).
- SLO-drift detection: detection can be implemented in the metrics pipeline (eg. compare rolling 7d baseline to 60m window + threshold). We should guard against alert fatigue: add debounce (1hr) and require at least X% traffic from a single variant before firing.

Estimate (rough):
- MVP detection + alert message: 2 backend sprints (ENG) + 1 sprint for notification templating.
- Route card UI + export endpoint: 1 frontend sprint + 1 backend sprint.
- Sampling retention increase or index: depends on scope — opt for index-by-route-id as incremental improvement (1-2 infra spikes).

Blockers: need agreement on retention policy and cost approval for any additional storage/indexing. Also need product to lock the alert semantics (thresholds, debounce).

I’ll add JIRA subtasks under ENG-1327 after the sync.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infra Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
